key_insight: Aggregate validation metrics (like perplexity) mask heterogeneous downstream scaling: some tasks improve with scale, others plateau, and some even degrade — so validation perplexity alone cannot reliably predict per-task performance.
problem_solved: Explains why predicting individual downstream task performance from average token-level validation loss fails, and provides analysis and alternatives to reveal and model diverse task-specific scaling behaviors.
method: Empirical analysis of many downstream tasks across model scales to characterize per-task scaling patterns (monotonic improvement, plateauing, degradation).

Diagnose two failure modes of using validation perplexity: (1) averaging token-level loss obscures informative signals; (2) no simple parametric scaling family captures the diversity of task behaviors.

Propose richer predictors and flexible fitting strategies (e.g., token-loss distribution summaries, nonparametric/mixture fits and per-task curves) and practical evaluation guidelines for model selection.
impact: Enables practitioners to better anticipate when scaling will help—or hurt—specific tasks, avoid overreliance on perplexity for model selection, and design more informative evaluation pipelines that reveal task-specific scaling.
visual_elements: Overlay plot: smooth aggregate validation loss power-law curve vs. multiple individual task curves showing improvement, plateau, and degradation.
Heatmap or cluster diagram grouping tasks by scaling behavior (improve/plateau/degrade).
Violin or histogram plots of token-level loss distributions to show how averaging hides signal.
Evaluation pipeline flowchart recommending per-task curve fitting, alternative predictors, and decision points for model selection.
paper_authors: Michael Y. Hu, Jane Pan, Ayush Rajesh Jhaveri, Nicholas Lourie, Kyunghyun Cho
